$description: Studio's global base and its semantic token layer, as a Jx style block. `styles/tokens.css` is GENERATED from this by `scripts/build-styles.ts`; edit this file and run `bun run styles:sync`. It stays a linked stylesheet because every declaration in it is pre-paint: the kit's own theme is adopted from JavaScript, so these hex fallbacks are what paints the shell before that lands. THE LAST OF `styles/spectrum.css` IS HERE. That file was the whole of what was declared ON the `sp-theme` element, where Spectrum's own ramp was in scope and `:root` was not, and its header said it would be deleted whole when that element went. It has: the box is `#shell-root` in `shell-frame.json`, the typography is the four declarations above (the sans stack is the kit's and 12px is `--jx-text-md`, which is what `--spectrum-font-size-75` resolved to), and `--case-c`/`--slot-c` are aliases in the same idiom as `--switch-c`, at the values `panel-outline.json` had already written down as their fallbacks. THE FOUR `--canvas-*` STEPS DO NOT FOLLOW THE THEME, and that is the point of them rather than an oversight: they colour surfaces that render as a light DOCUMENT in both chromes — the stylebook, the element-card previews, the empty-slot placeholder on the canvas — so they are mixed from the `black` and `white` KEYWORDS, which is what `var(--spectrum-black)`/`var(--spectrum-white)` were. Seven more steps were declared beside them and no rule in the package ever read one, so those are not here. The four `--data-*` syntax colours are not here either, for a reason `panel-data.json` states outright: nothing read them, they were declared for a palette nobody wrote, and `data-tone` still carries the type on every value for the day somebody does.
